title: Aggregator

validation.research: Six primary sources: Hohpe and Woolf’s Aggregator catalog entry; Spring Integration Aggregator documentation; Apache Camel Aggregate 4.22 documentation; RabbitMQ acknowledgments/publisher confirms; and Martin Fowler’s Event Aggregator and DDD Aggregate articles. The messaging pattern is defined through correlation, completeness, and combination. Message Aggregator is a descriptive search alias; DDD Aggregate and subscription-indirection Event Aggregator are explicitly distinct. Framework-specific defaults are not presented as universal guarantees. Messaging and Integration is the sole primary home.

runnable_example.verification: Six arrival permutations with repeated members and a zero-unit report; exact complete fixture and order-independent sum; conflicting open-group duplicate rejection without replacement; before/at/after deadline fixtures; no-input polling and zero deadline; sorted missing members and no misleading partial total; retained frozen terminal outcomes and no second local release; copied expected membership; 1/100-member boundaries and 0/101/duplicate-member rejection; 0/1000-unit bounds and malformed/Boolean/range rejection; operation/member isolation and identifier grammar/length; invalid clock rejection without state mutation; independent instances explicitly have no persistent deduplication history.

example_limits: Original one-group packing-result simulation. One operation ID has a fixed copied set of 1..100 distinct expected line IDs; ASCII identifiers are 1..64 characters. Authorized input reports 0..1000 packed physical units; complete means every expected member reported, not order fulfillment. Calls are sequential on a nondecreasing integer monotonic millisecond clock starting at zero. Identical open-group duplicates do not advance membership; conflicting open-group duplicates are rejected. The commutative sum is arrival-order independent. A fixed absolute deadline expires at now_ms >= deadline_ms; timeout records sorted missing members with total_units None. Each instance releases at most one frozen outcome and retains it, never reopening for valid late messages. The caller schedules polling and preserves state/configuration through the API. Empty work is handled upstream. No broker, durable state, restart recovery, global active-group bound, source authentication, concurrency control, automatic timer, cancellation, reliable output handoff, or exactly-once effect guarantee.
